title: Temperature Converter: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Temperature Converter: Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Temperature Converter](/temperature-converter) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin. Enter your temperature and from and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like. It is one of the [Conversion tools](/tools?category=Conversion) on CalcHub — the others work the same way.

Convert temperatures instantly between Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin — for cooking, travel, weather and science. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Conversion tools include [Length Unit Converter](/unit-converter), [Weight Converter](/weight-converter) and [Area Converter](/area-converter). People also look for this tool as "celsius to fahrenheit", "fahrenheit to celsius", "c to f".

## How to use the Temperature Converter

Start by entering your temperature, then choosing your from from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your temperature.
2. Choose your from from the list.
3. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
4. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

°F = °C × 9/5 + 32. °C = (°F − 32) × 5/9. K = °C + 273.15.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Temperature Converter](/temperature-converter) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 25 °C = 77 °F = 298.15 K. Body temperature 98.6 °F = 37 °C. Try the same figures in the [Temperature Converter](/temperature-converter) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Temperature: 25, From: Celsius (°C)), the [Temperature Converter](/temperature-converter) returns Celsius: 25 °C, Fahrenheit: 77 °F, Kelvin: 298.15 K. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Length Unit Converter](/unit-converter) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Quick estimate: double °C and add 30 for °F.
- −40 is the same in Celsius and Fahrenheit.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is 180 °C in Fahrenheit?

356 °F — a common oven temperature. Try it with your own numbers in the [Temperature Converter](/temperature-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is Kelvin ever negative?

No. 0 K is absolute zero. Try it with your own numbers in the [Temperature Converter](/temperature-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Temperature Converter use?

°F = °C × 9/5 + 32. °C = (°F − 32) × 5/9. K = °C + 273.15. You can see it in action in the [Temperature Converter](/temperature-converter) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Temperature Converter?

Just Temperature and From. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
